stem:
Pooja takes a steel tumbler of chilled lemonade out of the fridge on a humid afternoon. Small water droplets soon form on the outside of the tumbler.

Where do those outside droplets come from?

options.text: Water vapour from the surrounding air cools on the tumbler and turns into liquid water.
Water vapour from the air turns into droplets on the tumbler by evaporation.
Water vapour forms outside droplets on any tumbler it touches, even a warm one fresh from washing.
The tumbler becomes cold because vapour turns into droplets on it.

teacher.key_rationale: Outside droplets are condensation of airborne vapour on a cold surface. That change is not evaporation; a warm glass will not collect them the same way; coldness enables condensation rather than resulting from it.
